task: my recipe serves 4 and I need it for 11. original: 500g chicken thighs, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 150g rice, 300ml stock. scale everything and tell me if the pan size will be a problem.
rewrite:
ambition: A good cook scales by weight with a factor of 2.75 (11 ÷ 4), not by eye. They also know three things don't scale linearly. Paprika and salt start around 2x and get tuned by taste. Chicken browned in one crowded layer steams instead of searing, so it gets seared in batches or on a hot sheet tray. Evaporation depends on pan width, so stock is set by the rice ratio and not by the multiplier.

agency: The raw material is your actual pan, not a guess about "a big pan". Fill it with water and measure it in litres, then check its diameter and whether it has a lid. The other source is the rice packet's own water-to-rice ratio. If you can't measure the pan now, I'll assume a standard 28 cm deep sauté pan of about 4 L and flag it.

acceleration: Multiply every ingredient by 2.75 on a kitchen scale, using grams and ml in place of cups and spoons. Estimate the cooked volume as the sum of chicken, tomatoes, stock and rice at about 2.5x its dry volume. Use the oven as a second heat source: sear in batches, then finish covered at about 180°C as a one-pot pilaf. This avoids stovetop hot spots in a big pan.

accuracy: Fill your pan with water to its working line (about two-thirds full) and compare it with the calculated cooked volume. Use a probe thermometer to confirm the chicken reaches 75°C at the thickest piece. The rice should be tender with the liquid fully absorbed, and the dish should be tasted for salt before serving. If the pan fails the volume check, the proxy is to split it into two pans or one pan plus an oven dish.

answers.plain:
Scale factor: 11 ÷ 4 = 2.75

| Ingredient | Original (4) | Scaled (11) |
|---|---|---|
| Chicken thighs | 500 g | 1,375 g (~1.4 kg) |
| Olive oil | 2 tbsp | 5½ tbsp |
| Onion | 1 | 2¾ → 3 medium (or 2 large) |
| Garlic | 3 cloves | 8 cloves |
| Crushed tomatoes | 400 g (1 can) | 1,100 g (2¾ cans, so 3 cans and a little extra liquid is fine) |
| Smoked paprika | 1 tsp | 2¾ tsp (about 1 tbsp) |
| Rice | 150 g | 412 g (~410 g) |
| Stock | 300 ml | 825 ml |

**Pan size: yes, it will likely be a problem.**

- The original is probably in a 28 cm skillet or a medium pot. At 2.75x the volume, the finished dish is roughly 3.5 to 4 litres. That won't fit in a standard pan and would overflow many pots.
- Browning 1.4 kg of chicken in one layer needs about 40 cm of pan. In a normal pan, the chicken will crowd, steam, and not brown.
- Rice needs even contact with the liquid and an even heat. In a deep, crowded pot, the rice can cook unevenly.

**Options:**
1. **Best: use a large, wide pan.** A 12-quart Dutch oven or a 40 cm paella-style pan works. Brown the chicken in 2 batches anyway.
2. **Oven method.** Brown the chicken in batches on the stove, then build everything in a roasting tray or large casserole (about 30x40 cm). Cover tightly with foil and bake at 180°C for about 40 to 45 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through (75°C inside).
3. **Two pans.** Make two batches, roughly 5-6 servings each, in your regular pan. This is the lowest-risk option if you don't own a big pan.

**Tips for the scale-up:**
- Don't scale the liquid fully if you're using a wide, shallow pan, because there's less evaporation in a large covered pot. Start with about 750 ml of stock and add the rest only if the rice is still hard.
- Scale the salt and paprika gradually. Add about 2x first, then taste.
- Cooking time for the rice stays about the same (15 to 20 minutes), but the pot takes longer to come up to heat, so allow extra time for the early steps.
answers.nudge:
# Scaling to 11 servings (×2.75)

## Ingredients

| Ingredient | Original (4) | Scaled (11) | Practical amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chicken thighs | 500 g | 1375 g | **1.4 kg** (about 10–11 boneless thighs) |
| Olive oil | 2 tbsp | 5.5 tbsp | **4 tbsp** to start, plus a splash if the pan looks dry (see note 1) |
| Onion | 1 | 2.75 | **3 medium** |
| Garlic | 3 cloves | 8.25 | **8 cloves** |
| Crushed tomatoes | 400 g | 1100 g | **2 cans + 300 g** from a third can (or use all 3 cans for a saucier dish) |
| Smoked paprika | 1 tsp | 2.75 tsp | **2½ tsp**, then taste (see note 2) |
| Rice | 150 g | 412 g | **410 g** |
| Stock | 300 ml | 825 ml | **700 ml** to start, with about 125 ml held back (see note 3) |
| Salt | not listed | not listed | About 1½–2 tsp total, adjusted at the end |

Per person this works out to 125 g chicken and 37 g dry rice. That's the same as the original, so portions are unchanged.

## Where straight multiplication goes wrong

1. **Oil.** Oil coats a pan surface. It doesn't scale with the number of servings. Use about 4 tbsp, and add more only if the chicken sticks.
2. **Paprika and garlic.** Spices and aromatics tend to taste stronger when scaled linearly, because they have more time to infuse a bigger volume. Start at 2½ tsp paprika and adjust at the end. Smoked paprika turns bitter if scorched, so add it to the onions on lower heat and stir for no more than 30 seconds before adding liquid.
3. **Stock.** Evaporation depends on the pan's surface area, not the volume of food. A deeper, crowded pot loses proportionally less liquid, so 825 ml will probably leave the rice soggy. Start with 700 ml, and add the rest only if the rice is still firm and the pan is dry. The tomatoes also contribute liquid.
4. **Salt.** Season in stages. Salt the chicken, then the onions, then taste the sauce before the rice goes in. Stock saltiness varies a lot.

## Will the pan be a problem?

**Yes. This won't fit in the pan you'd use for 4.**

- **Volume.** The raw contents come to roughly 3.5–4 L, and the rice swells as it cooks. You need a vessel of at least **6 L**, and 7 L is safer so you can stir.
- **Rice depth.** Rice cooks evenly in a layer of about 3–4 cm. In a standard 28 cm skillet, this batch would be 8 cm or more deep. The bottom would scorch while the top stays hard.
- **Browning.** 1.4 kg of chicken won't brown in one layer in any normal pan. Crowded chicken steams and turns grey instead of browning.

### Options, best first

1. **Brown in batches, then finish in the oven (my pick).**
   - Brown the chicken in 3 batches in a wide pan, with a few minutes of resting between batches.
   - Build the sauce in the same pan, scraping up the browned bits.
   - Transfer everything to a **roasting tin or large casserole of about 35×25 cm and at least 6 cm deep**.
   - Stir in the rice and stock, cover tightly with foil, and bake at **190°C / 375°F for 40–45 minutes**.
   - Oven heat is even, so the rice won't scorch on the bottom.
2. **Two pans.** Split everything in half (each pan is ×1.375) and use two 28–30 cm skillets or sauté pans with lids. It's the simplest option if you don't own a big roasting dish, and each pan behaves like the original recipe.
3. **One large pot (6–7 L Dutch oven or a 34 cm+ paella pan).** This works, but stir gently and often, and expect to rotate the pot over the burner. If it's a wide paella pan, don't stir the rice after it goes in.

## Adjusted method

1. Pat the chicken dry and salt it. Brown it in 3 batches over medium-high heat and set it aside. This takes about 15 minutes in total.
2. Lower the heat and soften the onions for 8–10 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the paprika for 30 seconds.
3. Add the tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the rice and 700 ml of hot stock, then taste for salt.
4. Nestle the chicken back in and cover. Cook in the oven as above, or on the stove at the lowest simmer for about 25–30 minutes.
5. **Check at 30 minutes.** If the rice is still firm and the dish is dry, add hot stock a splash at a time, then re-cover.
6. Rest it covered for 10 minutes off the heat. The rice finishes steaming and the chicken relaxes.
7. Thighs are done at 74°C, but they're more tender at 80–85°C, so don't worry about going a bit over.

## Other tips

- **Timing.** Chicken thighs braised in a larger batch can take 5–10 minutes longer. Go by tenderness, not the clock.
- **Hot stock.** Add the stock hot, not cold. A large volume of cold liquid stalls the cooking and makes the rice gummy.
- **Holding.** If you're serving 11 at once, it holds well covered in a 120°C oven for up to 30 minutes.
- **Hungrier crowd.** If your guests have big appetites, raise the rice to 500 g and the stock to about 850 ml total. The original is chicken-heavy and a bit light on starch.
answers.skill:
# Scaled recipe: 4 → 11 servings (×2.75)

**Assumed pan:** 28 cm diameter, 4 L sauté pan. You haven't measured it, so this is an assumption.

## Ingredients

| Ingredient | Original | ×2.75 | Kitchen amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chicken thighs | 500 g | 1,375 g | **1,400 g** |
| Olive oil | 2 tbsp (30 ml) | 82 ml | **80 ml** (about 5½ tbsp), split across browning batches |
| Onion | 1 | 2.75 | **3 onions** (about 500 g peeled) |
| Garlic | 3 cloves | 8.25 | **8 cloves** |
| Crushed tomatoes | 400 g | 1,100 g | **3 cans (1,200 g)**. This is slightly more than the multiplier gives and is easier than part-using a can. |
| Smoked paprika | 1 tsp | – | **2 tsp** (about 2x, a starting amount) |
| Salt | – | – | **2 tsp** (about 10 g), a starting amount |
| Rice | 150 g | 412 g | **400 g** (a round figure, within 3% of the multiplier) |
| Stock | 300 ml | see below | **about 850 ml** |

Paprika and salt don't scale linearly. Start at about 2x, then taste at the end and adjust. Add more paprika in small pinches.

## Stock, set by the rice's absorption ratio

The original uses 300 ml stock for 150 g rice, a ratio of 2 ml per g. Scaling by the multiplier alone would give 825 ml. The tomatoes also contribute liquid, so I checked the stock against the rice.

- Rice: 400 g × 2 ml/g = **800 ml** of liquid needed for the rice.
- The original already includes the tomato liquid in its balance. The tomato scales from 400 g to 1,200 g (×3) while the rice only scales ×2.67, so the tomato is slightly heavy relative to the rice.
- Tomato excess: about 1,200 g − (400 g × 2.67 = 1,067 g) ≈ 133 g, so I trim the stock by about the same amount.
- Stock = (rice-based 2 ml/g × 400 g = 800 ml) + (extra evaporation allowance for a larger, fuller pan, about 50 ml) ≈ **850 ml**.

If you keep the multiplier alone, 825 ml is nearly identical. Use **850 ml** and keep a further 100 ml hot on the side. Add it only if the rice is still firm after the liquid is absorbed.

## Estimated total cooked volume

- Chicken: about 1,400 g, roughly 1.3 L
- Tomatoes, onion and oil: about 1.2 L + 0.45 L + 0.08 L ≈ 1.7 L
- Rice, which swells to about 2.5× its dry volume (400 g ≈ 0.5 L dry): about 1.25 L
- Stock: 0.85 L, of which most is absorbed into the rice and so is already counted in its swollen volume

Adding these gives about 4.3 L, and allowing for the stock absorbed into the rice, **the finished dish is roughly 4–4.5 L**.

## Will your pan work?

**No, not as a single pan.** A 4 L pan has a brim capacity of 4 L, and a pot should be no more than about two-thirds full for simmering rice. That means a working volume of about 2.7 L. At 4–4.5 L, the dish is far over.

**Needed for one pot:** a vessel of about **6.5–7 L**, roughly **30–32 cm in diameter** if it is a wide, shallow pan, or a 7 L Dutch oven or large casserole.

## Options

1. **Split across two pans (best with your gear).** Divide everything in half: 700 g chicken, 200 g rice, about 425 ml stock, 1½ onions, 4 cloves, 1½ cans tomato, 1 tsp paprika and 1 tsp salt. Each batch is about 2.1 L, which fits your 4 L pan. Use a second pan of a similar size.
2. **Oven finish.** Brown the chicken and build the sauce on the hob. Move it all to a large roasting tin or casserole (at least 7 L, with a lid or foil). Add the rice and hot stock, cover tightly and bake at 180°C for about 30–35 minutes.
3. **Hob and tray:** Brown the chicken in batches, make the sauce in the pan, then put everything in a deep tray in the oven.

## Browning without crowding

Brown the chicken in **3–4 batches** of about 350–450 g. Each piece needs a gap around it, and the pan floor should be about 60% covered at most. Use about 20 ml of the oil per batch, heat it until it shimmers, and leave each piece for 3–4 minutes per side without moving it. Set the browned pieces aside on a plate. Don't wash the pan, because the fond (browned bits) is flavour for the sauce.

## Checks

1. **Pan-capacity test with water.** Fill your pan to the brim with measured water, using a 1 L jug. Count the litres. For a 4 L pan this is your real maximum, and the working fill line is two-thirds of it. If the pan holds less than 4 L, use the split method.
2. **Chicken at 75°C.** Probe the thickest thigh away from the bone. Every piece must read 75°C or more.
3. **Rice tender, liquid absorbed.** The grains should be soft with no chalky centre and no pooling liquid. If it is still firm, add hot stock 50 ml at a time, cover and cook 5 more minutes.
4. **Salt taste.** Taste the sauce and rice at the end and adjust the salt and paprika then.

## The one measurement that would tighten this

**Your pan's real capacity in litres**, from the water test. It would confirm whether you need one pan or two.
